title: Small Hours
summary: A three-minute film for No. 9 Journal’s night issue. Two sisters get ready for a party that never starts. We shot it in one flat over two nights, mostly by the light of a fridge and a bathroom mirror.

images.alt: Film still: two women at a kitchen table at night, lit by an open fridge
A woman in a satin slip sitting on the edge of a bath, holding earrings
images.caption: Fitting, second night

images.alt: A hallway mirror with two blurred figures passing
A pile of borrowed dresses on an unmade bed
Close portrait of a woman with mascara running, looking at the camera

title: Lent
summary: Twelve pages for Mara Editions, issue 6. Everything is borrowed: from friends, from my mother, from a parish jumble sale. I wrote each lender’s name on a tag and left the tags in the shot.

images.alt: A woman in an oversized grey wool coat standing against a white wall, a paper tag hanging from the sleeve
Two women seated on church chairs, one in a lace collar, one in a cardigan buttoned wrong
images.caption: Collar lent by Odette Lisle

images.alt: Detail of hands holding a folded handkerchief over a pleated skirt
A woman lying on a parquet floor in a velvet dress, eyes closed
A clothes rail in an empty hall with handwritten tags on every hanger

title: The Long Lunch
summary: The SS25 campaign for Studio Ferrand. I cast the founder’s family and friends and set a lunch in their garden in the Drôme that ran from noon until the light went. Jonas photographed whoever was still at the table.

images.alt: A long table under plane trees, half-finished plates and twelve people in linen
An older man in a cream shirt laughing, holding a peach
A child asleep across two chairs under a striped jacket
images.caption: Four in the afternoon

images.alt: Wine glasses and a crumpled napkin on a white tablecloth
A woman in a pale yellow dress walking away down a gravel path
The empty table at dusk with chairs pushed back

title: Hothouse
summary: Photographs made in a municipal glasshouse during the winter it closed for repairs. I went in once a week from November to March. Some of these were published in Revue Plein Air; the prints are available as an edition of ten.

images.alt: Fogged glass with the shape of a palm frond pressed against it
Rows of potted orchids under plastic sheeting
A gardener’s green apron hanging on a rusted hook
Condensation running down a pane above a fern
Pale winter light through broken panes onto an empty walkway

title: Pale Fire
summary: Music video for Celeste Amaro’s single. One take in a closed ballroom, a red dress that loses a layer every verse. I built the dress in four pieces with the costume maker Hélène Vasseur so it could come apart on cue.

images.alt: Film still: a woman in a red dress alone on a ballroom floor
The red dress on a dress form with four detachable panels laid beside it
images.caption: The dress in four parts

images.alt: Celeste Amaro mid-turn under a chandelier, skirt blurred
A swatch card of red silks pinned with notes

title: Sunday Best
summary: Lookbook for Atelier Rovel’s autumn collection. The brief was church clothes worn on a Monday, so we shot in a laundrette and a bus shelter in Saint-Ouen.

images.alt: A woman in a navy pleated dress and white socks sitting on a laundrette bench
A man in a three-piece suit holding a carrier bag in a bus shelter
Two figures folding a white tablecloth between them
Detail of a patent shoe and a laddered stocking

title: Girls in the Orchard
summary: Forty-eight Polaroids made over two summers at my aunt’s farm in Normandy, of my cousins and their friends. Shown at Galerie Hesse in 2022, hung in a single line at hip height.

images.alt: Polaroid of a girl in a cotton nightdress standing between apple trees
Polaroid of three girls lying in long grass, faces turned away
The gallery wall with the Polaroids hung in one long row
images.caption: Installation, Galerie Hesse

images.alt: Polaroid of a hand holding a bruised apple
Polaroid of a ladder against a tree at dusk

title: Mother’s Wardrobe
summary: An inventory of my mother’s clothes from 1974 to 1999, photographed flat and then worn by my sister. Self-published as a 120-page book in an edition of 200.

images.alt: A brown corduroy skirt laid flat on white paper with a handwritten date
A young woman wearing the same corduroy skirt on a staircase
An open spread of the book showing a blouse and its receipt
images.caption: Spread, pages 46–47

images.alt: A floral summer dress pinned to a wall

title: Interiors
summary: Autumn catalogue for Maison Lune. They wanted the house to look lived in, so we moved in for a week: unmade beds, a half-read newspaper, a coat on the wrong chair.

images.alt: A bedroom with linen sheets pulled back and a cardigan on the floor
A ceramic jug of dried hydrangeas on a windowsill
A kitchen table with breakfast left out and morning sun across it
A wool blanket folded over the arm of a green sofa

title: Swim Season
summary: My first job under my own name: a swimwear lookbook for Ondine, shot in one day on a borrowed boat off Marseille. Towels, hats and sandals came from my own drawers.

images.alt: A woman in a red one-piece sitting on the deck of a small boat
Two swimmers climbing up a ladder from dark blue water
A striped towel and a straw hat drying on a rail
A woman with wet hair wrapped in a white robe, squinting at the sun
